var_pretty: Households Considered Mortgage Burdened
% of Households Considered Mortgage Burdened
national_summary_text: The U.S. Census defines owner or mortgage burden as those who spend more than 30 percent of their income on housing costs for homeowners. This data is general to the population and is an indicator of housing affordability in a location.
universe_note: Owner-occupied households in the state that carry a mortgage. A household is "mortgage burdened" when selected monthly owner costs take 30% or more of household income. This measure covers all such households and is not broken out by disability.
pct_definition: Of the state's owner-occupied households with a mortgage, the share paying 30% or more of household income toward selected monthly owner costs. Covers all such households, not only those with a disabled member.

var_pretty: Households Considered Rent Burdened

pct_definition: Of the state's renter-occupied households, the share paying 30% or more of household income toward gross rent (rent plus utilities). Covers all renter households, not only those with a disabled member.
